items.claim: The rejected-alternative argument mischaracterizes the tier of the boundary it sets aside, and three of the span's WEB citations reproduce a multi-verse open quotation as if each verse closed its own quotation mark.
items.evidence: The pe triplet runs Lam.3.46-Lam.3.48 by the acrostic letter data, a tier-1 warrant on its own footing; the rejected-alternative sentence instead attributes that triplet boundary to 'tier-3 parashah-mark symmetry' alone. A SAMEKH mark does fall at Lam.3.48 (tier-3, single-witness), but it corroborates the triplet boundary rather than constituting it, so the real comparison is a tier-1 pronoun shift against a tier-1 triplet boundary, not against a tier-3 signal; the medium_low confidence label is an appropriate hedge, but the prose understates how contested the cut is. Separately, the folded WEB text shows Lam.3.42 and Lam.3.46 each opening on a curly quote of their own that is never closed within that verse, with the matching close arriving only inside Lam.3.47's own text, and Lam.3.47 itself carrying no opening mark. This span's citations instead give Lam.3.42 and Lam.3.46 a closing curly quote neither carries and give Lam.3.47 an opening curly quote it does not carry, mismatched against the staged folded text at three of the span's four WEB citations.

items.claim: The justification for opening mid-triplet at Lam.3.48 labels the pe triplet's own formal grouping a tier-3 signal when the triplet boundary is itself a tier-1 warrant.
items.evidence: The pe triplet (Lam.3.46-Lam.3.48) is a triplet of the acrostic letter spine, a tier-1 structural unit on the same footing as every other triplet in the chapter. The boundary_rationale calls the grouping that includes the two verses left behind 'a tier-3 signal', conflating the triplet's own tier-1 status with the separate, real tier-3 SAMEKH mark that happens to close it at Lam.3.48. The pronoun-shift ground for cutting inside the triplet is a legitimate tier-1 reason, and the medium_low confidence with the frontier flag is an appropriate hedge, but the prose understates that the rejected alternative is tier-1, not tier-3.

items.claim: The qof and resh triplets (Lam.3.55-Lam.3.57, Lam.3.58-Lam.3.60) are tiled as complete triplets on an address-based tier-1 seam, and every quotation checks out at byte tier.
items.evidence: Each Hebrew splice (Lam.3.55, Lam.3.57, Lam.3.58) matches the byte text exactly, and the WEB quotations, including the nested “Don’t be afraid.” quotation at Lam.3.57, reproduce the folded text's own existing marks rather than adding new ones. The span opens and closes on full triplets, no triplet is cut, and the rejected alternative (extending back into the tsade triplet) is weighed against the genuine tier-1 address shift at Lam.3.55 without mischaracterizing either side's tier.

items.claim: The shin and tav triplets (Lam.3.61-Lam.3.63, Lam.3.64-Lam.3.66) close the triple acrostic exactly at the poem seam, with accurate quotations and an honestly disclosed shift into imprecation.
items.evidence: The three Hebrew splices (Lam.3.64, Lam.3.65, Lam.3.66) and both WEB quotations match the byte text exactly. The span ends where the 66-verse acrostic itself ends, so no triplet is cut, and the sole PE mark in the whole triple acrostic falls correctly at Lam.3.66, named against its true count of 1 of 66 verses. The shift from petition-report to imperative imprecation beginning at Lam.3.64 is disclosed as an operative-category deviation rather than left under a plain label.

items.claim: The span splices Hebrew and quotes WEB text from Lam.4.3, a doubled ketiv/qere verse, with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere in the row, and the disposition treating this as immaterial should be refuted rather than confirmed.
items.evidence: The byte text at Lam.4.3 carries two ketiv/qere doublets bracketing the phrase this span quotes, one unpointed-then-vocalized pair for the word rendered 'jackals' and a second for the word rendered 'like the ostriches', matching the verse's two entries in the ketiv/qere inventory. The span's device_notes splice the 'daughter of my people' phrase from this same verse and its boundary_rationale quotes the WEB rendering of the verse, yet no field in the row discloses the ketiv/qere status. The rule requiring disclosure for any splice from a ketiv/qere verse carries no materiality exception, so the omission is a real, confirmed defect rather than a false-positive heuristic trip, even though the specific quoted phrase itself falls outside the two variant word-pairs.

items.claim: The span's quotations and acrostic-letter disclosure are accurate at byte tier, and its divine-name claim holds under an independent check of the surrounding verses.
items.evidence: The Hebrew splices at Lam.4.7 and Lam.4.11 and both WEB quotations match the byte text exactly. The disclosed letters (zayin through kaf, positions seven through eleven) match the acrostic letter data for Lam.4.7-Lam.4.11. Checking every verse from Lam.4.7 through Lam.4.10 confirms the divine name does not occur until the span's own close at Lam.4.11, and the next occurrence is correctly pointed to Lam.4.16, so the claim that the name is named once in this group is accurate rather than assumed.
